candidates.change_summary: Replace the success check `require(_s)` with a constant `true` in the return expression, making the function always return true regardless of sub-call success.
Replace the require(_tos.length > 0) guard with require(_tos.length >= 0), making the function return true for empty input arrays instead of reverting.
Replace keccak256("transferFrom(address,address,uint256)") with keccak256("transfer(address,uint256)") so the external call targets a different selector.
Change loop increment from i++ to i += 2 so only every other recipient receives the transfer.
Change loop bound from i<_tos.length to i<=_tos.length, causing an out-of-bounds array access and revert on every call.
Swap the argument order in the external call to (from, v, _tos[i]) via abi.encodeWithSelector(id, from, v, _tos[i]).
Replace require(_s) with require(!_s) so successful external calls now cause a revert and failed calls proceed.
Ignore the external call success flag by using the tuple element for a different purpose: require(_s) becomes a no-op check on emit; instead replace return true with return false.
Change line 6 from require(_tos.length > 0) to require(_tos.length >= 0), making the precondition always true.
Change the function selector string from transferFrom(address,address,uint256) to transferFrom(address,address,uint256)  with an extra space, making the external call selector different.
Change line 8 loop condition from i<_tos.length to i<=_tos.length, causing an out-of-bounds access and behavior change for empty arrays.
Change line 9 to use tos[0] in every external call instead of the loop index i.
Change line 9 to ignore the success flag from the external call by removing the require(_s) check.
Change the final return from true to false.
Remove the require check for _tos.length > 0, allowing calls with empty array.
Delete the require(_s) inside the loop, so failed external calls do not revert the transaction.
Always return false instead of true at the end.
Change the function selector to `transfer(address,uint256)` so the external call targets a different function.
Insert a selfdestruct at the end so the contract is destroyed after one successful call.
Change the loop bound to `_tos.length - 1` so the last element is never processed.
Change the loop counter to start at 1, skipping the first element.
Delete the require(_tos.length > 0) precondition so zero-length _tos no longer reverts.
Replace the transferFrom selector with the ERC20 transfer selector, so calls encode transfer(address,uint256) instead of transferFrom(address,address,uint256).
Change the loop bound from i<_tos.length to i<=_tos.length, causing an out-of-bounds access that reverts.
Start the loop index at 1, so when _tos.length == 1 the call is skipped and no external call is made.
Insert a continue when i==0, skipping the first transfer call.
Swap the _tos[i] and v arguments in the call encoding, so the callee receives the wrong transfer arguments.
Make the success-check require fail on success instead of failure, inverting the external call result handling.
Delete the require(_s) check so failed external calls no longer revert.
Return false instead of true, changing the return value of a successful call.
Replace the requirement that _tos.length > 0 with _tos.length >= 0, removing the non-empty input guard.
Replace the transferFrom selector hash string with transfer(address,uint256), causing the external call to use a different function selector.
Replace the zero-initialized loop counter with a one-initialized counter, skipping the first target address.
Replace the loop bound from _tos.length with _tos.length - 1, skipping the last target address.
Remove the require(_s) check on the external call success flag, ignoring failed transfers.
Replace the success require(_s) with require(!_s), inverting the success condition.
Replace the final return true with return false, changing the function's success return value.
